compiled_state.description:
## Summary

The `Reconcile Bridge` "Commit reconciler events back and push to origin/tickets"
step exhausts its 5 retries and fails the workflow red under normal `tickets`-branch
contention. Spun out of bug `449f-f9bf-be90-47fe` (mode 2), whose fix covered the
other two failure modes; this one is separated because it changes retry semantics of
a shared push path and needs a contention harness to test honestly.

Two distinct defects, plus a disposition question.

## Defect 1 — the backoff is anti-adaptive for this failure class

`.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml:328`:

```sh
backoff=$(( (1 << attempt) + RANDOM % 3 ))
```

By the time this sleep runs, the loop has **already** fetched and merged
`origin/tickets` (`:321`), so its HEAD is a valid fast-forward *at that instant*. The
only thing that can invalidate it is another push landing first. Sleeping therefore
monotonically increases the probability of losing the very race the retry exists to
win — and the sleep **grows** (3 → 6 → 10 → 17s) exactly as the remaining attempt
budget shrinks.

Exponential backoff is correct for load-shedding against an overloaded or
rate-limited server. It is the wrong algorithm for an optimistic-concurrency CAS on a
hot append-only ref, where the correct move after a successful merge is to re-push
**immediately**.

## Evidence — full retry timeline recovered from run 30585738860

Every one of the five rejections is preceded by a *successful* merge and a
*successful* remote-tracking advance. The merges converge; only the push loses.

```
22:13:23.7  pre-loop fetch                      60ccc6506..4d37b6925
22:13:24.2  attempt 1 rejected (non-fast-forward)
22:13:24.7  merge OK (ort), "Waiting 3s"
22:13:28.3  attempt 2 rejected                  4d37b6925..dd70be0d7
22:13:29.0  merge OK, "Waiting 6s"
22:13:35.5  attempt 3 rejected                  dd70be0d7..a46013f4c
22:13:36.2  merge OK, "Waiting 10s"
22:13:46.7  attempt 4 rejected                  a46013f4c..f3a1fe61f
22:13:47.5  merge OK, "Waiting 17s"
22:14:05.0  attempt 5 rejected                  f3a1fe61f..939e92676
22:14:05.7  merge OK — never pushed, loop exits, exit 1
```

Derived: five remote advances over 41.9s => mean competitor interval **~8.4s**.
Backoff budget 30-38s of a ~42s loop. Each remote advance lands *inside* the
corresponding sleep.

Modelled with Poisson competitors at lambda = 1/8.4s, the per-attempt loss
probabilities are 35% / 54% / 72% / 88%, giving **P(all five fail) ~= 12% per run**.
With no sleep (window ~0.6s) the same model gives **~1.7e-6**.

Observed rate is consistent: 4 failures on 2026-07-30 clustered in contention bursts.

## Defect 2 — the final merge is computed and then discarded

`.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml:296-332`: the loop body is
`push -> classify -> fetch -> merge -> (if attempt < max) sleep`. On attempt 5 it
performs a full fetch+merge and then falls out of the `while` **without ever pushing
that merge**. The log above shows it: `f3a1fe61f..939e92676` is merged at 22:14:05.7
and the next line is `Push failed after 5 retries`.

That discarded merge had, by construction, just produced a fast-forwardable HEAD — a
free ~93%-likely attempt thrown away. Five pushes cost five merges and used four.

## The authority this violates

The workflow states its own intent at `:315-320`: the merge-not-rebase choice
"mirrors the local client path (`_store/push.py`) and invariant I1
(`docs/concurrency.md`)". The path it claims to mirror has **no backoff at all** —
`src/rebar/_store/push.py:167-210` re-pushes immediately on the next iteration after
`merge.returncode == 0 -> continue`. The workflow deviates from its stated reference
implementation in precisely the dimension that determines convergence.

## Open question — is red even the right disposition?

`docs/concurrency.md:297-300` states the contract for this operation: "Push is
**best-effort**: a failed push (no network, unresolvable non-fast-forward, recovery
state) **never fails the caller** — it warns, leaves local commits intact, and the
branch stays diverged. `rebar fsck` surfaces that divergence as a `PUSH_PENDING`
notice ... so it is not silent." `push.py:265` and `:286-291` implement exactly that:
warn, return, raise nothing.

The workflow instead exits 1. It has no `PUSH_PENDING` equivalent, so the missing
artifact may be the notice channel rather than the severity.

Counter-consideration that must be settled first, NOT assumed: the runner is
ephemeral, so a lost push discards the merged local commits with the container, while
the Jira-side mutations were already applied. Whether that is benign depends on
whether the next pass re-derives the same events. `docs/jira-sync-setup.md:151-154`
suggests it does ("a pass that times out makes no durable progress and the next pass
re-does the work"), but that is about a timed-out pass, not a lost push.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Decide and record whether an exhausted push race should be red or a
      `PUSH_PENDING`-style non-red notice, resolving it against
      `docs/concurrency.md:297-300` rather than by preference. Evidence required:
      confirm for the 4 failed runs (30503669644, 30510284129, 30515516036,
      30585738860) that the events they failed to push were re-derived by a later
      pass, and that no duplicate Jira issue was created for the same `local_id`.
- [ ] Retry-after-successful-merge no longer sleeps an increasing interval; the
      re-push after a clean merge is immediate (matching `_store/push.py`).
      Any retained delay is justified in a comment against a named failure mode.
- [ ] The final merge is either pushed or not computed — no iteration performs a
      merge whose result is provably discarded.
- [ ] A deterministic contention harness covers this: a scripted competitor that
      pushes before each attempt, asserting the loop converges rather than
      exhausting. RED against the current loop first.
- [ ] Measured: over >= 500 subsequent `Reconcile Bridge` runs, zero failures
      attributable to push-race exhaustion (`gh run list` evidence).
- [ ] File paths: `.github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml` (lines 294-335);
      `src/rebar/_store/push.py` if the budgets are reconciled (it uses 3, the
      workflow 5).
compiled_state.title: Reconcile Bridge push retry: exponential backoff is anti-adaptive for a CAS race, and the final merge is computed then discarded
